# Lookup Table and Case Reduction
## Overview
Builds on [Marching Cubes Lookup and Configuration](2518-marching-cubes-lookup-and-configuration.md) [G]. This family covers algorithmic modifications to Marching Cubes that reduce lookup table size through symmetry or decompose ambiguous configurations into simpler primitives [G]. It sets itself apart from sibling methods like [Snap Marching Cubes](2181-snap-marching-cubes.md) by focusing on combinatorial reduction and topological disambiguation rather than geometric snapping [G].
## Shared principles
Not given in the sources.
## Subtopics

### [Sub-case decomposition for n-dimensional marching cubes](11668-sub-case-decomposition-for-n-dimensional-marching-cubes.md)
Reduces configuration space complexity in $n$-dimensions by decomposing major cases into edge-connected sub-cases. It sets itself apart from sibling methods by explicitly handling topological ambiguities through geometric decomposition into simplices rather than relying solely on symmetry reduction or displacement mapping. It uses an orientation matrix (32-bit integer, 2 bits per position) to map primary table entries to secondary table simplices. In 3D, it identifies 14 major cases and 74 sub-cases; in 4D, 222 major cases. Tetrahedronization uses a "fewest edges" heuristic, with backtracking required for only 3 of 74 sub-cases in 3D. Ambiguities are handled via separate complementary case configurations and vertex ordering.

### [Improved Marching Cubes with New Table and Displacement](14182-improved-marching-cubes-with-new-table-and-displacement.md)
Improves the worst-case triangle quality of Marching Cubes by combining a modified lookup table that avoids specific edge groups responsible for poor triangles with a non-linear displacement of cut points on edges. It sets itself apart from standard Marching Cubes by explicitly optimizing for triangle aspect ratio bounds rather than just topological correctness. It uses a gain function parameter $k=0.3$ to modulate the normalized position of cut points, applying greater displacement closer to endpoints. Unavoidable bad triangles remain in some cases (e.g., convex polygons must include edge group 2), and improvement trades off with triangles that already have good aspect ratios.

### Generic Rule Marching Cubes
A variant of Marching Cubes that uses a single generic rule to triangulate all 15 standard cube configurations and additional cases, eliminating the need for a lookup table [S1]. It resolves the Type A ‘hole problem’ which occurs when at least one cube face has an intersection point in each of its four edges [S1]. Tested on full resolution CT and MRI of human heads on SGI Indigo 2 with 128 MB RAM [S1]. Differs from standard Marching Cubes by not requiring definition of different cube configurations, rotations, or comparisons with predefined configurations, reducing execution time [S1].
